meaning: Aaron's age when he and Moses confronted Pharaoh; otherwise without prominent symbolic meaning
description: The number 83 has no broad symbolic meaning in biblical tradition like the numbers 7, 12, or 40. The most direct biblical occurrence is in Exodus 7:7, where it is told that Aaron was eighty-three years old when he and Moses spoke to Pharaoh. Aaron's age here marks the beginning of God's mighty deliverance of Israel from Egypt, and emphasizes that God calls and uses people regardless of age. Beyond this reference, the number 83 is not attributed any special symbolic value in Jewish or Christian tradition.

versions.meaning: The number 83 has no prominent or well-established symbolic significance in biblical or Jewish tradition.
versions.description: The number 83 does not appear as a symbolically important number in the Bible or in traditional Jewish numerology (gematria) in the same way as numbers like 7, 12, 40, or 613. Psalm 83 is known as a prayer for protection against Israel's enemies, but the number 83 itself is not attributed any independent symbolic value. In gematria, various Hebrew words may sum to 83, but none of these have given the number a widely recognized symbolic status in tradition.

footnotes.text: Psalm 83 is a prayer attributed to Asaph, in which the author calls on God not to remain silent while a coalition of nations conspires against Israel. The psalm is counted among the so-called imprecatory psalms (prayers against enemies).

In gematria (the Hebrew system of numerical values), the number 83 can arise from summing various Hebrew words, but none of these have given the number a widely recognized symbolic status in rabbinic or kabbalistic literature.

According to rabbinic chronology, Aaron was three years older than Moses (Exod 7:7). Their respective ages (83 and 80) at the start of their mission before Pharaoh highlight that both were advanced in age, underscoring that the power behind the deliverance came from God, not from human youthful strength.
